Before you present

Four useful checks

  1. Keep credits, source information and speaker notes with reused slides.
  2. Check facts against the source review date and ask the content or science owner about changes in meaning.
  3. Check contrast, reading order and alternative text; caption video.
  4. Check the presentation on the actual display or delivery format.

Reuse, adapt or ask?

Use released material within its usage notes. Ask the content owner about changed claims; ask Creative Production about substantial design work.

Brand essentials

Use these digital values from the retained SKAO Brand Book v2, March 2022.

Blueshift Navy #070068
Redshift Magenta #E70068

Apply colour carefully

  • Use navy for text and links on light backgrounds. Magenta works well as an accent; check each text/background pairing.
  • For print, use the Brand Book and the supplier’s agreed colour specifications rather than guessing CMYK or Pantone conversions.
  • Use labels, symbols or patterns as well as colour to communicate meaning.

title: Agree scope and timing
keywords:
Planning the work

Give the actual use date and explain what depends on it. Delivery timing is agreed after the brief and capacity are reviewed.

Send the brief

What affects the schedule

  • The output, complexity and amount of adaptation required.
  • Who reviews the work and when they can respond.
  • Supplier production, delivery and other dependencies.

An urgent request?

State the real deadline, its reason and what can be reduced. Urgency does not automatically create a delivery commitment.

Where are templates and slides?

Where are photos and video?

Can I adapt material myself?

Who approves the work?

Identify the appropriate content owner and final reviewer in the brief. The approval route depends on the work and should be confirmed rather than assumed.

Can I get an urgent turnaround?

title: Format a presentation
keywords:
Self-service guide

Start with a suitable template and build the talk around your audience.

Find presentation resources

Build the story

  • Give each slide a clear purpose and use readable, concise headings.
  • Use the supplied layouts and keep spacing, alignment and typography consistent.
  • Use imagery and charts to explain the message; retain their sources and credits.

Check before presenting

  • Try the deck on the intended display and check that text and charts are readable from the audience’s position.
  • Check contrast, alternative text and reading order. Caption any video.
  • Check facts, dates and any adapted claims with the appropriate content owner.

title: Accessibility checks
keywords:
Make the work usable

Build accessibility into the document or presentation, then check the exported result.

Content and structure

  • Use clear headings, descriptive links and a logical reading order.
  • Give informative images alternative text that conveys their purpose. Decorative images should be ignored by assistive technology, for example with empty alt text in HTML.
  • Caption video and provide an appropriate text alternative for audio.

Appearance and interaction

  • Use readable contrast: WCAG’s minimum is generally 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text.
  • Do not rely on colour alone. Use labels, symbols or patterns too.
  • Check keyboard access and focus visibility for interactive content.

Check the relevant standard

These checks are a starting point, not a claim that the work passes a full accessibility audit.
